ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: What is the name of the colorless plastid that forms starch granules and occurs in cells of plant storage tissue?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: The image shows a schematic diagram of a plant cell structure: the cell is rectangular and has a relatively thick green outer boundary, inside there are multiple green oval organelles similar to chloroplasts, a very large central vacuole, a cell nucleus in the blue area, and labels for other cell structures such as mitochondria and Golgi apparatus. This confirms that the question is in the biological context of plant cells and organelles/plastids. The question asks: what is the colorless plastid that appears in plant storage tissue cells and can form starch grains called. Colorless plastids belong to leucoplasts, among which the one that specifically synthesizes and stores starch is the starch body, namely amyloplast.
